findings.title: Type-check enum fields before testing set membership
findings.snippet:
require(entry.get("decision") in DECISIONS, ...)
require(entry.get("execution_class") in EXECUTION_CLASSES, ...)
findings.failure_scenario: Load an otherwise valid catalog with an entry whose decision or execution_class is an array or object; invoke main(["--json", "--repo-root", fixture_root, "list"]).
observed_evidence: decision=[] raised TypeError: unhashable type: list and produced empty stdout.
execution_class=[] produced the same uncaught exception and empty stdout.
The public CLI catches IntegrationError and OSError only, so these malformed catalog inputs bypass its structured error response.
findings.impact: A malformed catalog crashes the CLI and breaks JSON consumers instead of returning the existing INVALID_CATALOG error envelope.
findings.requested_change: Require a string value before membership checks for both fields, and add negative CLI tests asserting a structured INVALID_CATALOG response and exit code 2 for array/object values.

findings.title: Enforce the packet budget as each payload is loaded
findings.snippet:
for resource in entry.get("resources", []):
    resource_content = self._content(...)
    payloads.append((resource_target, resource_content))
    total += len(resource_content)
require(total <= MAX_PACKET_BYTES, ...)
findings.failure_scenario: Select one valid skill with many individually valid resources whose combined size exceeds MAX_PACKET_BYTES. Every resource is read and retained before the packet limit is checked. The notice loop similarly postpones its budget check until all notices have been loaded.
observed_evidence: A fixture with a 110-byte entrypoint, three 64-byte resources, and a temporarily reduced 142-byte packet limit read all 302 bytes before raising LIMIT_EXCEEDED; the first resource had already exceeded the budget.
Production constants permit 512 resources per entry and 16 MiB per file, allowing approximately 8 GiB of resource payloads to accumulate for one entry before the 128 MiB packet guard executes.
The current code keeps each bytes object in payloads, so the postponed check does not merely perform unnecessary reads; it retains the excess allocation.
findings.impact: Oversized but well-formed input can exhaust memory and terminate the process before it can return the intended LIMIT_EXCEEDED failure.
findings.requested_change: Check the aggregate limit immediately after each entrypoint, resource, and notice read, before retaining or reading further payloads. Prefer bounding each read by the remaining packet budget when practical. Add a regression test asserting that later resources/notices are not read after the budget is exhausted.

validation.additional_checks: Standard-library temporary fixtures reproduced both reported failures. No dependency installation, network access, third-party source execution, or source-file edits were performed.

summary.verdict_basis: The supplied reviewer role permits approval when no CRITICAL or HIGH findings are present. Both MEDIUM findings should be addressed for production failure robustness.
